newsitem.title: GERMANY: FedEx sees future Russia air cargo growth.
newsitem.headline: FedEx sees future Russia air cargo growth.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said it foresees steady growth in the Russian air cargo imports and exports make up to the end of the century.
The freight integrator said it expected the Russian express parcels export market to grow 40 percent a year from 3,000 parcels a day over the next few years.

FedEx managing director Germany Antje Schuett, said at a news conference in Frankfurt: "We see the economic situation in Russia as relatively stable and growth potential means it is important to establish ourselves there."
"We hope strongly that when the rouble becomes convertible, exports will pick-up," she added.
The country's GDP was projected to increase to $224 billion in 2000 or 32 percent up from 1996, with exports rising 27 percent to 25.3 billion dollars, Schuett said.
"Russian exports are destined 32 percent for western Europe and 34 percent of imports come from western Europe," she noted.
Eastern Europe and CIS states made up 33 percent of Russian exports and 40 percent of imports, she added.

FedEx started Tuesday a five day a week Boeing 727-200 flight with 25 tonnes freight capacity from Paris via Frankfurt to Moscow Vnukovo airport with a return flight via Munich to Paris. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
